### What the results say

### Overview

- A 2PL model with 1 dimension was fitted to 600 respondents and 32
  items (EM estimation).
- The estimation converged normally.

### Model fit

- Overall model fit is close: M2 = 683.96, df = 464, RMSEA = 0.028, CFI
  = 0.953, SRMSR = 0.045.
- The chi-square test is significant, but with large samples this is
  common; the RMSEA indicates the misfit is small in practical terms.

### Reliability

- Marginal reliability is 0.84 (good).

### Targeting

- The average item location is -0.01 and the average person score is
  -0.00, so the test is well targeted for this group.
- Measurement is most precise around theta = -1.20 (information = 7.19,
  SE = 0.37).

### Items

- Low discrimination: Item.12 (a = 0.16), Item.30 (a = 0.39), Item.32 (a
  = 0.13). These items barely separate high and low scorers; review the
  key and wording.
- Extreme location: Item.9 (b = -4.04), Item.11 (b = -3.03), Item.21 (b
  = -4.15), Item.32 (b = 12.75). These items are far too easy or too
  hard for most respondents.
- Low item-total correlation: Item.9 (r = 0.13), Item.11 (r = 0.16),
  Item.12 (r = 0.08), Item.21 (r = 0.14), Item.30 (r = 0.16), Item.32 (r
  = 0.04). These items relate weakly to the rest of the test.
- Misfit: Item.22 (S-X2 p = .004), Item.25 (S-X2 p \< .001). The model
  does not describe responses to these items well (alpha = 0.01);
  inspect them with gg_empirical() or item_card().

### Local dependence

- No item pairs show signs of local dependence (Q3).

### Person fit

- 3.0% of respondents have unusual response patterns (Zh \< -1.96),
  which is within what chance alone would produce.
